title.en: Volume 92 Book of Later Jin 18: Biographies 7 - Yao Yi, Lu Qi, Liang Wenju, Shi Gui, Pei Hao, Wu Chengfan, Lu Dao, Zheng Taoguang, Wang Quan, Han Yun, Li Yi
title.raw: 卷九十二 晉書18: 列傳七 姚顗 呂琦 梁文矩 史圭 裴皞 吳承範 盧導 鄭韜光 王權 韓惲 李懌 Volume 92 Book of Later Jin 18: Biographies 7 - Yao Yi, Lu Qi, Liang Wenju, Shi Gui, Pei Hao, Wu Chengfan, Lu Dao, Zheng Taoguang, Wang Quan, Han Yun, Li Yi

sentences.zh: 姚顗，字伯真，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Yao Yi, styled Bozhen, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi, whose courtesy name was Bozhen, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖希齊，湖州司功參軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xiqi was Registrar of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xiqi had served as registrar in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖宏慶，蘇州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hongqing was Prefect of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hongqing had been prefect of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父荊，國子祭酒。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing had been rector of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 顗少蠢，敦厚，靡事容貌，任其自然，流輩未之重，唯兵部侍郎司空圖深器之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: As a youth Yi was dull yet honest and thick; he paid no heed to appearance and let nature take its course. His peers did not esteem him; only Vice Minister of War Sikong Tu deeply appreciated him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yi seemed slow-witted yet was honest and unassuming; he cared nothing for his looks and let things be. Contemporaries paid him little heed, but Sikong Tu, vice minister of war, valued him deeply and married his daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 顗性仁恕，多為仆妾所欺，心雖察之，而不能面折，終身無喜怒。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature benevolent and forgiving. Servants and concubines often deceived him; though he perceived it in his heart, he could not confront them to their faces, and throughout his life he showed neither anger nor joy.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was gentle and forgiving by nature. Servants and concubines often took advantage of him; he saw it clearly enough, yet could never rebuke them openly, and he went through life without showing anger or delight.

sentences.zh: 不知錢百之為陌，黍百之為銖，凡家人市貨百物，入增其倍，出減其半，不詢其由，無擔石之儲，心不隕獲。

translations.literal: He did not know that a hundred coins make a string (mo) or that a hundred grains of millet make a zhu. Whenever household members bought or sold anything, they doubled the price on receipt and halved it on payment; he never inquired why. Though he had no store of grain worth a dan or shi, his heart did not sink at the loss.
translations.idiomatic: He did not know that a hundred coins make a string or a hundred grains of millet a zhu. When the household bought or sold, they doubled every incoming price and halved every outgoing one, and he never asked why. He had scarcely a bushel of grain in store, yet his spirit did not break under the waste.

sentences.zh: 唐末，隨計入洛，出遊嵩山，有白衣丈夫拜於路側，請為童仆。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, he accompanied the examination delegation to Luoyang. While touring Mount Song, a man in white robes bowed by the roadside and asked to serve as his boy attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tang he went to Luoyang for the metropolitan examination and visited Mount Song. A man in white bowed beside the road and asked to become his servant.

sentences.zh: 顗辭不納。

translations.literal: Yi declined and would not accept him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi refused and would not take him in.

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「鬼神享於德，君子孚於信。

translations.literal: The man then said: "Ghosts and spirits partake of virtue; the gentleman stands upon good faith.
translations.idiomatic: The man then said, "Ghosts and spirits feed on virtue; the gentleman lives by faith.

sentences.zh: 余則鬼也，將以托賢者之德，通化工之信，幸無辭焉。

translations.literal: I am a ghost, and wish to rely upon a worthy man's virtue and communicate the transforming power of Heaven's trust—please do not refuse."
translations.idiomatic: I am a ghost, and wish to rest upon a worthy man's virtue and carry Heaven's transforming trust—please do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 昔余掌事陰府，承命攝人之魂氣，名氏同而其人非，且富有壽算，復而歸之，則筋骸已敗，由是獲譴，使不得為陽生。

translations.literal: Long ago I administered affairs in the dark underworld. I received orders to take charge of people's souls and vital spirits. When names were the same but the persons were not, and the soul still had ample allotted lifespan, returning it found the sinews and bones already decayed. For this I received punishment and was forbidden to live as a yang being among the living.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago I served in the realm of darkness, charged with taking souls. When the name matched but not the person, and the allotted years were still many, the body I returned to was already ruined. For that I was punished and barred from living among men.

sentences.zh: 公中夏之相輔也，今為謁中天之祠，若以某姓名求之，神必許諾。

translations.literal: You are a minister who will aid China in its central lands. Now you are going to offer prayers at the Central Heaven shrine. If you petition there using a certain name, the spirits will surely grant it."
translations.idiomatic: You are destined to aid the central realm. You are now going to pray at the shrine of the Central Heaven. If you plead there under a certain name, the spirits will surely grant it."

sentences.zh: 」顗因為之虔禱而還，白衣迎於山下，曰：「余免其苦矣。

translations.literal: Yi therefore prayed fervently on his behalf and returned. The man in white met him at the foot of the mountain, saying: "I am released from my suffering."
translations.idiomatic: Yi prayed earnestly for him and returned. The man in white met him at the foot of the mountain and said, "I am freed from my torment."

sentences.zh: 」拜謝而退。

translations.literal: He bowed in thanks and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed in thanks and went away.

sentences.zh: 顗次年擢進士第。

translations.literal: The following year Yi passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Yi passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，歷校書郎、登封令、右補闕、禮部員外郎，召入翰林，累遷至中書舍人。

translations.literal: During the Zhenming era of Liang, he successively served as Collator, Magistrate of Dengfeng, Right Remonstrator, and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites; he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy and was promoted in stages to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang in the Zhenming era he served as collator, magistrate of Dengfeng, right remonstrator, and vice director of rites, entered the Hanlin Academy, and rose step by step to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，以例貶復州司馬，歲餘牽復，授左散騎常侍，歷兵吏部侍郎、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang conquered Liang, he was demoted by precedent to Military Governor's Aide at Fuzhou; after more than a year he was recalled and appointed Left Regular Attendant, then served successively as Vice Minister of War, Vice Minister of Personnel, and Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong of Tang overthrew Liang, Yi was demoted by precedent to aide at Fuzhou; after a year he was recalled, made left regular attendant, and later served as vice ministers of war and personnel and as left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 唐末帝即位，講求輔相，乃書朝中清望官十餘人姓名置於瓶中，清夜焚香而挾之，既而得盧文紀與顗，遂拜中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Modi of Tang acceded, he sought out counsellor-assistant ministers. He wrote the names of more than ten officials of pure reputation in court on slips, placed them in a jar, and at night burned incense and drew one out. He obtained Lu Wenji and Yi, whereupon they were appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Chief Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Modi of Tang came to the throne he sought chief ministers. He wrote the names of a dozen eminent officials on slips, put them in a jar, burned incense at night, and drew one out. Lu Wenji and Yi were chosen, and both were made vice director of the secretariat and chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 制前一日，嵩山白衣來謁，謂顗曰：「公明日為相。

translations.literal: The day before the edict of appointment, the man in white from Mount Song came to visit Yi and said: "Tomorrow you will become chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of the appointment edict, the man in white from Mount Song came to see him and said, "Tomorrow you will be chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」其言無差，冥數固先定矣。

translations.literal: His words were not off by a hair; fate in the dark realms had indeed been fixed beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: His words proved exact; what was ordained in the unseen had long been settled.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，罷相為刑部尚書，俄遷戶部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Yi was dismissed as chief minister and made Minister of Justice, then soon transferred to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Yi was removed as chief minister and made minister of justice, then soon minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 天福五年冬卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died in the winter of the fifth year of Tianfu, at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in winter of the fifth year of Tianfu, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子惟和嗣。

translations.literal: His son Weihe succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Weihe succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 顗疏於財，而禦家無術，既死，斂葬之資不備，家人俟賻物及鬻第方能舉喪而去。

translations.literal: Yi was indifferent to wealth yet had no skill in managing his household. After his death, funds for burial were not prepared; his family had to wait for condolence gifts and the sale of the residence before they could conduct the funeral and depart.
translations.idiomatic: Yi cared little for money and knew nothing of household management. After his death there was not enough for burial; his family had to wait for gifts of condolence and the sale of the house before they could bury him and leave.

sentences.zh: 士大夫愛其廉而鄙其拙。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials admired his integrity but scorned his ineptitude.
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters admired his integrity but despised his helplessness.

sentences.zh: 呂琦，字輝山，幽州安次人也。

translations.literal: Lu Qi, styled Huishan, was a native of Anci in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, courtesy name Huishan, was from Anci in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，瀛州景城主簿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou was Registrar of Jingcheng in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou had been registrar of Jingcheng in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父兗，滄州節度判官，累至檢校右庶子。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Military Governor's Judge at Cangzhou and rose in stages to Supernumerary Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been military judge at Cangzhou and rose to supernumerary right guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 劉守光攻陷滄州，琦父兗被擒，族之。

translations.literal: When Liu Shouguang captured Cangzhou, Qi's father Yan was seized and his entire clan executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shouguang took Cangzhou, Qi's father Yan was captured and the whole clan put to death.

sentences.zh: 琦時年十五，為吏追攝，將就戮焉。

translations.literal: Qi was then fifteen; officials pursued and seized him, and he was about to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was fifteen at the time; officers seized him and he was about to be killed.

sentences.zh: 有趙玉者，幽、薊之義士也，久遊於兗之門下，見琦臨危，乃紿謂監者曰：「此子某之同氣也，幸無濫焉。

translations.literal: There was a man named Zhao Yu, a man of righteousness from You and Ji, who had long been associated with Yan's household. Seeing Qi in peril, he deceived the guard, saying: "This boy is my younger kinsman—pray do not kill him indiscriminately."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhao Yu, a champion of You and Ji who had long been in Yan's service, saw Qi in danger and lied to the guard: "This boy is my kinsman—please do not kill him by mistake."

sentences.zh: 」監者信之，即引之俱去。

translations.literal: The guard believed him and led Qi away together with him.
translations.idiomatic: The guard believed him and led Qi away with him.

sentences.zh: 行一舍，琦困於徒步，以足病告，玉負之而行，逾數百里，因變姓名，乞食於路，乃免其禍。

translations.literal: After traveling one stop, Qi grew weary of walking on foot and pleaded foot ailment. Yu carried him on his back for several hundred li. They changed their names and begged food along the road, and thus escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: After one stage on the road Qi could walk no farther and pleaded a foot ailment. Yu carried him on his back for hundreds of li. They changed their names and begged along the way, and so escaped death.

sentences.zh: 年弱冠，以家門遇禍，邈無所依，乃勵志勤學，多遊於汾、晉。

translations.literal: When he reached the capping age, bereft of family after the calamity and with nowhere to turn, he resolved to study diligently and traveled widely in Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, his family destroyed and with nowhere to turn, he threw himself into study and traveled widely through Fen and Jin.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，莊宗方開霸府，翹佇賢士，墨制授琦代州軍事判官，秩滿歸太原，監軍使張承業重琦器量，禮遇尤厚。

translations.literal: During the Tianyou era of Tang, Zhuangzong was just establishing his hegemon's headquarters and eagerly awaited worthy men. By informal edict Qi was appointed Military Judge at Daizhou. When his term ended he returned to Taiyuan; Commissioner Zhang Chengye valued Qi's character and capacity and treated him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianyou era Zhuangzong was opening his headquarters and sought worthy men. Qi was appointed military judge at Daizhou by informal edict. When his term ended he returned to Taiyuan, where Commissioner Zhang Chengye valued his character and treated him with special honor.

sentences.zh: 天成初，拜琦殿中侍御史，遷駕部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Qi was appointed Attending Censor within the Palace, then transferred to Vice Director of the Transport Bureau, concurrently serving as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiancheng he was made palace attending censor, then vice director of the transport bureau, and also attending censor in charge of miscellaneous cases.

sentences.zh: 會河陽帑吏竊財事發，詔軍巡院鞫之。

translations.literal: When a treasury clerk at Heyang was caught stealing funds, an edict ordered the Military Patrol Office to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When a treasury clerk at Heyang was caught stealing, the court ordered the military patrol office to investigate.

sentences.zh: 時軍巡使尹訓怙勢納賂，枉直相反，俄有訴冤於闕下者，詔琦按之，既驗其奸，乃上言請治尹訓，沮而不行。

translations.literal: The Military Patrol Commissioner Yin Xun relied on power and accepted bribes, inverting right and wrong. Soon someone appealed injustice at the imperial gate. An edict ordered Qi to investigate. Having verified the malfeasance, he submitted a memorial asking that Yin Xun be punished, but it was blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The patrol commissioner Yin Xun abused his power and took bribes, twisting justice. Soon someone appealed at the palace gates. Qi was ordered to investigate, proved the wrongdoing, and memorialized for Yin Xun's punishment, but the request was blocked.

sentences.zh: 琦連奏不已，訓知其不免，自殺於家，其獄遂明，蒙活者甚眾，自是朝廷多琦之公直。

translations.literal: Qi submitted memorial after memorial without ceasing. Xun knew he could not escape and killed himself at home. The case was then clarified and many who would have died were spared. From this time the court admired Qi's fairness and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Qi kept memorializing without stop. Xun knew he could not escape and killed himself at home. The case was cleared and many lives saved. From then on the court prized Qi's fairness.

sentences.zh: 高祖建義於太原，唐末帝幸懷州，趙德鈞駐軍於團柏谷，末帝以琦嘗在德鈞幕下，因令賫都統使官告以賜之，且犒其軍焉。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised the righteous cause at Taiyuan, Emperor Modi of Tang went to Huaizhou; Zhao Dejun encamped at Tuanbai Valley. Modi, knowing Qi had once served under Dejun, ordered him to deliver the Chief Commander's commission and proclamation as a gift and also to reward his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan, Emperor Modi went to Huaizhou while Zhao Dejun camped at Tuanbai Valley. Modi, knowing Qi had served under Dejun, sent him to present the chief commander's commission and reward the army.

sentences.zh: 及觀軍於北陲，館於忻州，會晉祖降下晉安寨，遣使告於近郡，琦適遇其使，即斬之以聞，尋率郡兵千人間道而歸。

translations.literal: When he went to review the army on the northern frontier, he lodged at Xinzhou. It happened that the Lord of Jin had reduced Jin'an Fortress and sent a messenger to inform nearby prefectures. Qi happened upon the messenger, immediately beheaded him and reported this, then led a thousand prefectural troops by a hidden route back to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting troops on the northern border he stayed at Xinzhou. The Lord of Jin had taken Jin'an Fortress and sent messengers to nearby prefectures. Qi met the messenger, beheaded him at once and reported it, then led a thousand prefectural troops back by a hidden road.

sentences.zh: 高祖入洛，亦弗之責，止改授秘書監而已。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Luoyang, he did not punish him either, but merely reassigned him to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Luoyang he did not punish him, but only reassigned him as director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 天福中，預修《唐書》，權掌選部，皆有能名焉。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he participated in compiling the Book of Tang and acted as head of the Personnel selection bureau—both brought him a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he helped compile the Book of Tang and headed personnel selection, winning a reputation for competence in both.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部、刑部、戶部、兵部侍郎，階至金紫光祿大夫，爵至開國子。

translations.literal: He was promoted in stages to Vice Minister of Rites, Punishments, Revenue, and War, reaching the rank of Grand Master of Golden Beryl Radiance and the title Viscount of a newly founded state.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the vice ministries of rites, punishments, revenue, and war, attaining grand master of golden beryl radiance and the title viscount of a newly founded state.

sentences.zh: 琦美風儀，有器概，雖以剛直聞於時，而內實仁恕。

translations.literal: Qi had fine bearing and breadth of character. Though famed in his day for stern integrity, inwardly he was truly benevolent and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had fine presence and breadth of spirit. Though known for stern integrity, at heart he was gentle and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖謀求輔相，時宰臣李崧力薦琦於高祖，雲可大用。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu was seeking chief ministers, the chief councillor Li Song vigorously recommended Qi to him, saying he could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was seeking chief ministers, Li Song strongly recommended Qi, saying he could be put to great use.

sentences.zh: 高祖數召琦於便殿，言及當世事，甚奇之，方將倚以為相，忽遇疾而逝，人皆惜之。

translations.literal: Gaozu repeatedly summoned Qi to the informal hall and discussed current affairs with him, finding him remarkable. He was about to rely on him as chief minister when Qi suddenly fell ill and died; all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often summoned him to the informal hall to discuss affairs of the day and found him extraordinary. He was about to make him chief minister when Qi fell ill and died suddenly; everyone mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 梁文矩，字德儀，鄆州人。

translations.literal: Liang Wenju, styled Deyi, was a native of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wenju, courtesy name Deyi, was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父景，秘書少監。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Vice Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing had been vice director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 梁福王友璋好接賓客，文矩少遊其門，初試太子校書，轉秘書郎。

translations.literal: Prince of Fu Youzhang of Liang delighted in receiving guests; Wenju as a youth frequented his gate. He first passed examination as Collator to the Heir Apparent, then was transferred to Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Youzhang of Fu in Liang loved to entertain guests; Wenju frequented his house in youth. He first passed as collator to the heir apparent, then became a secretary.

sentences.zh: 友璋領鄆州，奏為項城令，及移鎮徐方，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Youzhang held Yanzhou, he memorialized Wenju as Magistrate of Xiangcheng. When he transferred his command to Xuzhou, he recruited Wenju as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhang governed Yanzhou he recommended Wenju as magistrate of Xiangcheng. When he moved his command to Xuzhou he took Wenju on as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 友璋卒，改兗州觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Youzhang died, Wenju became Judge on the Staff of the Yanzhou Observation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After Youzhang's death he became judge on the Yanzhou observation staff.

sentences.zh: 時莊宗遣明宗襲據鄆州，文矩以父母在鄆，一旦隔越，不知存亡，為子之情，戀望如灼，遂間路歸鄆，尋謁莊宗。

translations.literal: At that time Zhuangzong sent Mingzong to seize Yanzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were at Yanzhou; suddenly cut off, he did not know whether they lived or died. Filial feeling burned in him like fire; he took a bypath back to Yanzhou and soon presented himself to Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong then sent Mingzong to take Yanzhou by surprise. Wenju's parents were there; cut off at once, he did not know if they lived or died. Filial longing burned like fire; he took a hidden road back to Yanzhou and soon presented himself to Zhuangzong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗喜之，授天平軍節度掌書記，在明宗幕下。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was pleased and appointed him Secretariat Secretary on the staff of the Tianping Military Commission, serving under Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong was pleased and made him secretariat secretary on the Tianping staff under Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 明宗歷汴、恒二鎮，皆隨府遷職。

translations.literal: As Mingzong served successively at the Bian and Heng prefectures, Wenju followed each transfer in office.
translations.idiomatic: As Mingzong served at Bian and Heng in turn, Wenju followed each posting.

sentences.zh: 天成初，授右諫議大夫，知宣武軍軍州事，歷御史中丞、吏部侍郎、禮部尚書、西都副留守，判京兆府事，縱改兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was appointed Right Advisory Censor, acting as military prefect of the Xuanwu Army; he successively served as Censor-in-Chief, Vice Minister of Personnel, Minister of Rites, Vice Defender of the Western Capital, adjudicating metropolitan affairs of Jingzhao, then was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiancheng he was made right advisory censor and acting military prefect of the Xuanwu army, then served as censor-in-chief, vice minister of personnel, minister of rites, vice defender of the western capital with jurisdiction over Jingzhao, and finally minister of war.

sentences.zh: 文矩以嘗事霸府，每懷公輔之望。

translations.literal: Because Wenju had once served the hegemon's headquarters, he always harbored hopes of becoming chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Having once served the hegemon's headquarters, he always hoped to become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時高祖自外鎮入覲，嘗薦於明宗曰：「梁文矩早事陛下，甚有勤勞，未升相輔，外論慊之。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu came from an outer command to pay court and once recommended to Mingzong: "Liang Wenju served Your Majesty early with great toil; he has not been raised to chief minister, and public opinion is dissatisfied."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu came from an outer command to pay court he once told Mingzong, "Liang Wenju served Your Majesty early with great labor; he has not been made chief minister, and public opinion is dissatisfied."

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「久忘此人，吾之過也。

translations.literal: Mingzong said: "I had long forgotten this man—it is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong said, "I had long forgotten this man—it is my fault."

sentences.zh: 」尋有旨降命，會丁外憂而止。

translations.literal: Soon an edict was about to descend appointing him, but he happened to enter mourning for his father and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an appointment edict was about to issue, but he entered mourning for his father and it was halted.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，拜太常卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qingtai he was made director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，授吏部尚書，改太子少師。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was made Minister of Personnel, then changed to Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he was made minister of personnel, then junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 文矩喜清靜之教，聚道書數千卷，企慕赤松、留侯之事，而服食尤盡其善。

translations.literal: Wenju delighted in the teachings of quiet purity. He collected several thousand volumes of Daoist books, aspired to the affairs of Master Redpine and the Marquis of Liu, and pursued ingestion of elixirs with utmost dedication.
translations.idiomatic: Wenju loved the way of quiet purity, gathered thousands of Daoist volumes, aspired to Master Redpine and the Marquis of Liu, and pursued elixirs with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 後因風痹，上章請退，以太子太保致仕，居洛陽久之。

translations.literal: Later, because of wind paralysis, he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and left office as Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent, residing in Luoyang for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Later, afflicted with wind paralysis, he memorialized to retire and left office as grand mentor to the heir apparent, living long in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 天福八年，以疾卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died of illness at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianfu he died of illness, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 史圭，常山人也。

translations.literal: Shi Gui was a native of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gui was from Changshan.

sentences.zh: 其先與王武俊來於塞外，因家石邑。

translations.literal: His ancestors came from beyond the frontier with Wang Wujun and thereafter made their home at Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears had come from beyond the frontier with Wang Wujun and settled at Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾，歷鎮陽牙校。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zeng served successively as military camp officer at Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zeng had served as camp officer at Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 父鈞，假安平、九門令。

translations.literal: His father Jun held acting appointments as Magistrate of Anping and Jimen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun had held acting appointments as magistrate of Anping and Jimen.

sentences.zh: 圭好學工詩，長於吏道。

translations.literal: Gui loved learning and was skilled in poetry and excelled in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gui loved learning and poetry and excelled in administration.

sentences.zh: 唐光化中，歷阜城、饒陽尉，改房子、寧晉、元氏、樂壽、博陸五邑令。

translations.literal: During Guanghua of Tang he served successively as Assistant Magistrate of Fucheng and Raoyang, then was transferred as Magistrate of five districts: Fangzi, Ningjin, Yuanshi, Leshou, and Bolu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang Guanghua he served as assistant magistrate of Fucheng and Raoyang, then as magistrate of Fangzi, Ningjin, Yuanshi, Leshou, and Bolu in turn.

sentences.zh: 為寧晉日，擅給驛廩，以貸饑民，民甚感之。

translations.literal: While magistrate of Ningjin, he on his own authority distributed relay-station grain stores to lend to famine victims; the people were deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Ningjin he on his own authority opened relay granaries to lend grain to the starving; the people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 及為樂壽令，里人為之立碑。

translations.literal: When he became Magistrate of Leshou, the villagers erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he became magistrate of Leshou, the villagers erected a stele in his honor.

sentences.zh: 同光中，任圜為真定尹，擢為本府司錄，不應命。

translations.literal: During Tongguang, when Ren Yuan was Metropolitan Governor of Zhending, he promoted Gui to Recorder of that prefecture, but Gui did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongguang, when Ren Yuan was metropolitan governor of Zhending, he offered Gui the post of recorder, but Gui declined.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜領其地，辟為從事，及明宗代崇韜，以舊職縻之。

translations.literal: Guo Chongtao took command of the region and recruited him as staff officer. When Mingzong replaced Chongtao, he retained Gui in his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao took the region and recruited him as staff officer. When Mingzong replaced Chongtao, he kept Gui in the same post.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，入為文昌正郎，安重誨薦為河南少尹，判府事，尋命為樞密院直學士。

translations.literal: When Mingzong acceded, Gui entered court as Principal Secretary in the Wenchang Bureau. An Chonghui recommended him as Vice Governor of Henan, adjudicating prefectural affairs, and soon he was appointed Direct Academician of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong came to the throne Gui entered court as principal secretary in the Wenchang bureau. An Chonghui recommended him as vice governor of Henan with jurisdiction over prefectural affairs, and soon he was made direct academician of the privy council.

sentences.zh: 時圭以受知於重誨，重誨奏令圭與同列閻至俱升殿侍立，以備顧問，明宗可之。

translations.literal: At that time Gui enjoyed An Chonghui's trust. Chonghui memorialized that Gui and his colleague Yan Zhi should both ascend the hall to stand in attendance as advisers-in-waiting. Mingzong approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gui then enjoyed An Chonghui's favor. Chonghui memorialized that Gui and his colleague Yan Zhi should both attend in the hall as advisers. Mingzong approved.

sentences.zh: 尋自左諫議大夫拜尚書右丞，有入相之望。

translations.literal: Soon from Left Advisory Censor he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with prospects of entering the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose from left advisory censor to right vice director of the secretariat, with prospects of becoming chief minister.

sentences.zh: 圭敏於吏事，重誨本不知書，為事剛愎，每於明宗前可否重務，圭恬然終日，不能剖正其事。

translations.literal: Gui was sharp in administrative matters, but Chonghui was fundamentally unlettered and was stubborn in conduct; daily before Mingzong he approved or rejected weighty business, and Gui sat calmly all day unable to analyze and correct these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was sharp in administration, but Chonghui was barely literate and obstinate; day after day before Mingzong he decided weighty affairs, and Gui sat calmly all day unable to set things right.

sentences.zh: 長興中，重誨既誅，圭出為貝州刺史，未幾罷免，退歸常山。

translations.literal: During Changxing, after Chonghui was executed, Gui went out as Prefect of Beizhou, was soon dismissed, and retired to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: During Changxing, after Chonghui was executed, Gui was sent out as prefect of Beizhou, soon dismissed, and retired to Changshan.

sentences.zh: 由是閉門杜絕人事，雖親戚故人造者不見其面，每遊別墅，則乘婦人氈車以自蔽匿，人莫知其心。

translations.literal: From this he shut his gates and cut off human contact. Though kin and old friends came calling, they did not see his face. Whenever he toured his villa he rode in a woman's felt carriage to conceal himself, and no one knew his mind.
translations.idiomatic: He then shut his doors to the world. Kin and old friends who called did not see his face. When he visited his villa he rode in a woman's felt carriage to hide himself, and no one knew what was in his heart.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，征為刑部侍郎，判鹽鐵副使，皆宰臣馮道之奏請也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended, Gui was summoned as Vice Minister of Punishments and Deputy Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Monopoly—all upon Chief Councillor Feng Dao's memorial request.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne Gui was summoned as vice minister of punishments and deputy salt and iron commissioner, all on Feng Dao's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 始圭在明宗時為右丞，權判銓事，道在中書，嘗以堂判衡銓司所註官，圭怒，力爭之，道亦微有不足之色，至是圭首為道所舉，方愧其度量遠不及也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gui was Right Vice Director under Mingzong, he acted as head of selection affairs. Feng Dao was in the Secretariat and once used his chief councillor's adjudication to override appointments the Selection Bureau had registered. Gui grew angry and fought it fiercely; Dao too showed a slight air of displeasure. Now Gui was the first whom Dao recommended, and he felt ashamed that his magnanimity fell far short of Dao's.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as right vice director under Mingzong, Gui had headed selection. Feng Dao in the secretariat once used his chief councillor's ruling to override the selection bureau's appointments. Gui grew angry and fought it; Dao too showed displeasure. Now Gui was the first Dao recommended, and he was ashamed that his breadth of spirit fell far short of Dao's.

sentences.zh: 旋改吏部侍郎，分知銓事，而圭素厲廉守節，大著公平之譽。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Vice Minister of Personnel and shared headship of selection affairs. Gui had always been strict in integrity and observance of duty, and won great repute for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made vice minister of personnel and shared headship of selection. Gui had always been strict in integrity, and won great fame for fairness.

sentences.zh: 圭前為河南少尹日，有嵩山術士遺圭石藥如鬥，謂圭曰：「服之可以延壽，然不可中輟，輟則疾作矣。

translations.literal: When Gui had earlier been Vice Governor of Henan, a Mount Song adept gave him a stone medicine like a peck measure in size, telling him: "If you take this you can prolong life, but you must not stop midway—if you stop, illness will arise."
translations.idiomatic: When Gui had been vice governor of Henan, a Mount Song adept gave him a stone medicine the size of a peck measure and said, "If you take it you can prolong life, but you must not stop midway—if you stop, illness will follow."

sentences.zh: 」圭後服之，神爽力健，深寶惜焉。

translations.literal: Gui later took it and felt spirits refreshed and strength robust; he treasured it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Gui later took it and felt clear in spirit and strong in body; he treasured it deeply.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，圭在常山，遇秘瓊之亂，時貯於衣笥，為賊所劫，後不復得。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, Gui was at Changshan when Mi Qiong's rebellion broke out. The medicine was then stored in his clothes chest and was plundered by bandits; he never recovered it afterward.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qingtai Gui was at Changshan when Mi Qiong's rebellion broke out. The medicine was in his clothes chest and was seized by bandits; he never recovered it.

sentences.zh: 天福中，疾生胸臆之間，常如火灼，圭知不濟，求歸鄉里，詔許之。

translations.literal: During Tianfu, illness arose in his chest and constantly burned like fire. Gui knew he would not recover and requested to return home. An edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu illness arose in his chest and burned like fire. Gui knew he would not recover and asked to return home; the court granted it.

sentences.zh: 及涉河，竟為藥氣所蒸，卒於路，歸葬石邑，時年六十八。

translations.literal: When he crossed the river, he was ultimately overcome by vapors from the medicine, died on the road, and was buried at Shiyi at the age of sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: When he crossed the river he was overcome by vapors from the medicine, died on the road, and was buried at Shiyi, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 裴皞，字司東，系出中眷裴氏，世居河東為望族。

translations.literal: Pei Hao, styled Sidong, descended from the central branch of the Pei clan, a prominent family long settled in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hao, courtesy name Sidong, came from the central branch of the Pei clan, a great family long settled in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 皞容止端秀，性卞急，剛直而無隱，少而好學，苦心文藝，雖遭亂離，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Hao's bearing was refined and elegant; his nature was impetuous, sternly upright and without concealment. From youth he loved learning and labored at literary arts; though amid turmoil and separation, his hand never left his scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's bearing was refined and elegant; he was quick-tempered, upright, and frank. From youth he loved learning and labored at letters; though amid turmoil he never put down his books.

sentences.zh: 唐光化三年，擢進士第，釋褐授校書郎，歷諫職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving the sackcloth he was appointed Collator and served in remonstrance offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tang Guanghua he passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving office dress he was made collator and served in remonstrance posts.

sentences.zh: 梁初，當路推其文學，遷翰林學士、中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang those in power promoted his literary accomplishment; he was transferred to Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Liang those in power prized his literary talent; he was made Hanlin academician and secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗時，擢為禮部侍郎，後以語觸當事，改太子賓客，旋授兵部尚書，以老致仕。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites; later because his words offended those in power, he was changed to Household Companion to the Heir Apparent, then soon made Minister of War, and retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhuangzong of Tang he was made vice minister of rites; later his words offended those in power and he was made household companion to the heir apparent, then minister of war, and retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 天福初，起為工部尚書，復告老，以右僕射致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he was recalled as Minister of Works, again requested retirement on account of age, and left office as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianfu he was recalled as minister of works, again asked to retire on account of age, and left office as right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皞累知貢舉，稱得士，宰相馬裔孫、維翰皆其所取進士也。

translations.literal: Hao repeatedly oversaw the metropolitan examination and was said to have obtained worthy men; chief councillors Ma Yisun and Wei Han were both jinshi he had selected.
translations.idiomatic: Hao repeatedly oversaw the metropolitan examination and was said to have chosen worthy men; chief councillors Ma Yisun and Wei Han were both jinshi he had selected.

sentences.zh: 後裔孫知貢舉，率新進士謁皞，皞喜，為詩曰：「詞場最重是持衡，天遣愚夫受盛名，三主禮闈年八十，門生門下見門生。

translations.literal: Later Yisun oversaw the examination and led the new jinshi to pay respects to Hao. Hao was pleased and composed a poem: "In the literary arena the weightiest thing is holding the scale; Heaven sends this foolish man to receive great fame—three times presiding over the Rites Gate, eighty years old, a disciple's disciple meets his disciple."
translations.idiomatic: Later Yisun oversaw the examination and led the new jinshi to visit Hao. Hao was pleased and wrote a poem: "In the literary arena the weightiest thing is holding the scales; Heaven sends this foolish man great fame—three times presiding over the Rites Gate, eighty years old, a disciple's disciple meets his disciple."

sentences.zh: 」當世榮之。

translations.literal: The age honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries took pride in it.

sentences.zh: 維翰嘗私見皞，皞不為迎送，人問之，皞曰：「我見桑公於中書，庶僚也；

translations.literal: Wei Han once visited Hao in private; Hao did not go out to welcome or see him off. When people asked about it, Hao said: "When I saw Lord Sang at the Secretariat, he was a fellow official;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Han once paid a private visit to Hao, who did not come out to welcome or escort him. When asked, Hao said, "When I saw Lord Sang at the secretariat, he was a colleague;

sentences.zh: 今見我於私第，門生也。

translations.literal: now he comes to see me at my private residence—he is a disciple."
translations.idiomatic: now he visits me at home—he is a disciple."

sentences.zh: 」聞者以為允。

translations.literal: Those who heard it thought this apt.
translations.idiomatic: Hearers judged this fair.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Grand Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand mentor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 承範溫厚寡言，善希人旨，桑維翰、李崧尤重之，嘗薦於高祖，雲可大用。

translations.literal: Chengfan was mild and sparing of words, skilled at discerning others' intent. Sang Weihan and Li Song especially valued him and once recommended him to Gaozu, saying he could be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfan was gentle and reticent, adept at reading others' wishes. Sang Weihan and Li Song prized him highly and once recommended him to Gaozu as fit for great use.

sentences.zh: 承範知之，持重自養，雖遇盛夏，而猶服襦袴，加之以純綿，蓋慮有寒濕之患也。

translations.literal: Chengfan knew this and cultivated gravity in self-care. Even in midsummer he still wore jacket and trousers lined with pure cotton, fearing ailments from cold and damp.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfan knew this and kept himself reserved. Even in midsummer he wore jacket and trousers padded with cotton, lest cold and damp harm him.

sentences.zh: 然竟不獲其志，其命也夫！

translations.literal: Yet in the end he did not realize his ambitions—it was fate!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he never attained his aims—such was his lot!

sentences.zh: 盧導，字熙化，其先范陽人也。

translations.literal: Lu Dao, styled Xihua, was by ancestry from Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dao, courtesy name Xihua, came of Fanyang stock.

sentences.zh: 祖伯卿，唐殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Boqing was Attending Censor within the Palace under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Boqing had been a palace attending censor under Tang.

sentences.zh: 父如晦，國子監丞，贈戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Ruhui was Assistant Director of the Imperial University; posthumously awarded Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ruhui had been assistant director of the imperial university and was posthumously made vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 導少而儒雅，美詞翰，善談論。

translations.literal: Dao from youth was refined and elegant, fine in literary composition, and skilled in discourse.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Dao was cultured and graceful, gifted in letters and skilled in conversation.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐初，登進士第，釋褐除校書郎，由均州鄖鄉縣令、入為監察御史，三遷職方員外郎，充史館修撰，改河南縣令禮部郎中，賜紫，轉右司郎中兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou of Tang he passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving the sackcloth he was made Collator, then served as Magistrate of Yunxiang in Junzhou, entered as Investigating Censor, was thrice promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments, served as Historiographer in the History Office, changed to Magistrate of Henan and Director of the Ministry of Rites, was granted purple robes, and transferred to Director of the Right Secretariat concurrently as Attending Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tang Tianyou he passed the jinshi, became collator, then magistrate of Yunxiang in Junzhou, entered as investigating censor, rose thrice to vice director of appointments, served as historiographer, became magistrate of Henan and director of rites, received purple robes, and became director of the right secretariat while also attending censor in charge of miscellaneous cases.

sentences.zh: 以病免，閑居於漢上，久之。

translations.literal: He resigned on account of illness and lived in retirement on the Han River for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced his retirement, and he lived quietly on the Han for many years.

sentences.zh: 天成中，以本官征還，拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng he was recalled at his former rank and appointed Right Advisory Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he was recalled and made right advisory censor.

sentences.zh: 長興末，為中書舍人，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: At the end of Changxing he was Secretariat Drafter and acted as head of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Changxing he was secretariat drafter and oversaw the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 明年春，潞王自鳳翔擁大軍赴闕，唐閔帝奔於衛州，宰相馮道、李愚集百官於天宮寺，將出迎潞王。

translations.literal: The next spring the Prince of Lu led a great army from Fengxiang toward the capital. Emperor Min of Tang fled to Weizhou. Chief councillors Feng Dao and Li Yu gathered the officials at Tiangong Temple to go out and welcome the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring the Prince of Lu marched from Fengxiang with a great army. Emperor Min of Tang fled to Weizhou. Feng Dao and Li Yu gathered officials at Tiangong Temple to go out and welcome him.

sentences.zh: 時軍眾離潰，人情奔駭，百官移時未有至者。

translations.literal: At that time the armies were scattered in defeat and the people fled in panic; for a long while no officials arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Armies were scattered and the people panicked; for a long while no officials came.

sentences.zh: 導與舍人張昭遠先至，馮道請導草勸進箋，導曰：「潞王入朝，郊迎可也；

translations.literal: Dao and Drafter Zhang Zhaoyuan arrived first. Feng Dao asked Dao to draft a memorial urging accession. Dao said: "When the Prince of Lu enters court, suburban welcome is enough;
translations.idiomatic: Dao and drafter Zhang Zhaoyuan arrived first. Feng Dao asked Dao to draft a memorial urging accession. Dao said, "When the Prince of Lu comes to court, a suburban welcome suffices;

sentences.zh: 若勸進之事，安可造次。

translations.literal: as for urging accession, how can we act rashly?
translations.idiomatic: as for urging him to take the throne, how can we act rashly?

sentences.zh: 且潞王與主上，皆太后之子，或廢或立，當從教令，安得不稟策母後，率爾而行！

translations.literal: Moreover, the Prince of Lu and the sovereign are both sons of the Empress Dowager. Whether to depose or to establish should follow her command—how can we fail to seek the Empress Dowager's decision and act on our own!"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the prince and the emperor are both the empress dowager's sons. Deposing or enthroning should follow her command—how can we act without her word!"

sentences.zh: 」馮道曰：「凡事要務實，勸進其可已乎？

translations.literal: Feng Dao said: "In all affairs one must be practical—can urging accession be stopped?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "In affairs one must be practical—can urging accession be set aside?"

sentences.zh: 」導曰：「今主上蒙塵在外，遽以大位勸人，若潞王守道，以忠義見責，未審何詞以對！

translations.literal: Dao said: "Now the sovereign suffers exile abroad; to hurry the great throne upon another—if the Prince of Lu holds to the Way and rebukes us for disloyalty, I do not know what words we could answer with!
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "The emperor is in exile abroad; to rush the throne upon another—if the prince holds to loyalty and rebukes us, what could we answer!

sentences.zh: 不如率群臣詣宮門，取太后進止，即去就善矣。

translations.literal: Better to lead the ministers to the palace gate, obtain the Empress Dowager's decision, and then choose the proper course."
translations.idiomatic: Better to lead the ministers to the palace gate, obtain the empress dowager's decision, and then act rightly."

sentences.zh: 」道未及對，會京城巡檢安從進報曰：「潞王至矣，安得百僚無班。

translations.literal: Before Dao could reply, the capital patrol commissioner An Congjin reported: The Prince of Lu has arrived—how can the hundred officials be without formation?
translations.idiomatic: Before Dao could answer, capital patrol commissioner An Congjin reported that the Prince of Lu had arrived—how could the officials be without formation?

sentences.zh: 」即紛然而去。

translations.literal: They at once scattered and left.
translations.idiomatic: They scattered at once and left.

sentences.zh: 是日，潞王未至，馮道等止於上陽門外，又令導草勸進箋，導執之如初。

translations.literal: That day the Prince of Lu had not yet arrived; Feng Dao and others stopped outside the Shangyang Gate and again ordered Dao to draft the accession memorial. Dao held to his view as before.
translations.idiomatic: That day the prince had not yet arrived; Feng Dao and others waited outside the Shangyang Gate and again asked Dao to draft the accession memorial. Dao held firm as before.

sentences.zh: 李愚曰：「舍人之言是也，吾輩信罪人矣。

translations.literal: Li Yu said: "The drafter's words are right—we are truly guilty men."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu said, "The drafter is right—we are truly guilty men."

sentences.zh: 」導之守正也如是。

translations.literal: Such was Dao's upholding of what was right.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Dao's steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，由禮部侍郎遷尚書右丞，判吏部尚書銓事，秩滿，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: During Tianfu of Jin he moved from Vice Minister of Rites to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, adjudicating selection affairs for the Minister of Personnel; when his term ended he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During Jin Tianfu he rose from vice minister of rites to right vice director of the secretariat, heading personnel selection; when his term ended he became vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，卒於東京，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he died in the Eastern Capital at the age of seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the sixth year he died in the eastern capital, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 鄭韜光，字龍府，洛京清河人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Taoguang, styled Longfu, was a native of Qinghe in the Luoyang capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Taoguang, courtesy name Longfu, was from Qinghe in the Luoyang region.

sentences.zh: 曾祖絪，為唐宰相。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yin was a chief councillor of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yin had been a Tang chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 祖祗德，國子祭酒，

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhide was Rector of the Imperial University,
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhide had been rector of the imperial university,

translations.literal: (Annotation:
translations.idiomatic: (Note:

sentences.zh: （《新唐書·宰相世系表》：祗德，兵部尚書。）〉

translations.literal: (New Book of Tang, "Tables of Chief Councillor Lineages": Zhide was Minister of War.)]
translations.idiomatic: (New Book of Tang, "Tables of Chief Councillor Lineages": Zhide was minister of war.)]

sentences.zh: 贈太傅。

translations.literal: posthumously awarded Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 父顥，河南尹，贈太師。

translations.literal: His father Hao was Metropolitan Governor of Henan; posthumously awarded Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hao had been metropolitan governor of Henan and was posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 其先世居滎陽，自隋、唐三百餘年，公卿輔相，蟬聯一門。

translations.literal: His forebears had long dwelt at Xingyang; for more than three hundred years from Sui through Tang, high ministers and chief councillors followed one another in a single clan.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long lived at Xingyang; for more than three hundred years from Sui through Tang, ministers and chief councillors had followed one another in a single house.

sentences.zh: 韜光，唐宣宗之外孫，萬壽公主之所出也，生三日，賜一子出身，銀章朱紱。

translations.literal: Taoguang was a maternal grandson of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, born of Princess Wanshou. On the third day after birth he was granted the status of a first son's entry into office, with silver seal and crimson sash.
translations.idiomatic: Taoguang was a grandson of Tang Xuanzong on the maternal side, born of Princess Wanshou. On the third day of life he was granted first-son entry into office, with silver seal and crimson sash.

sentences.zh: 及長，美容止，神爽氣澈，不妄喜怒，秉執名節，為甲族所稱。

translations.literal: When grown he had fine bearing, clear spirit and transparent air, showed neither anger nor joy without cause, held fast to reputation and integrity, and was praised by the foremost clans.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he had fine bearing and a clear, bright spirit; he did not show anger or joy without cause, held to honor, and was praised among the great families.

sentences.zh: 自京兆府參軍歷秘書郎、集賢校理、太常博士、虞部比部員外郎、司門戶部郎中、河南京兆少尹、太常少卿、諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: From Military Aide in the Jingzhao prefecture he served successively as Secretary, Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Vice Director in the Bureaus of Parks and Comparative Standards, Director in the Bureaus of Passes and Household Registration, Vice Governor of Henan and Jingzhao, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Advisory Censor, and Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from aide in Jingzhao through secretary, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, doctor of imperial sacrifices, vice directors in parks and comparative standards, directors in passes and household registration, vice governor of Henan and Jingzhao, vice director of imperial sacrifices, advisory censor, and drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，懇求休退，上表漏名，責授寧州司馬。

translations.literal: During Zhenming of Liang he earnestly sought retirement; his memorial omitted his name and he was punished by appointment as Military Governor's Aide at Ningzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang Zhenming he earnestly sought retirement; his memorial omitted his name and he was demoted to aide at Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平梁，遷工、禮、刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong conquered Liang, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works, Rites, and Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong overthrew Liang he was made vice minister of works, rites, and punishments.

sentences.zh: 天成、長興中，歷尚書左右丞。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng and Changxing he served successively as Left and Right Vice Directors of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng and Changxing he served as left and right vice directors of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 國初，以戶部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he retired as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he retired as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 自繈褓迄於懸車，凡事十一君，越七十載，所仕無官謗，無私過，三持使節，不辱君命，士無賢不肖，皆恭己接納。

translations.literal: From swaddling clothes to hanging up his carriage, he served eleven rulers over more than seventy years. In office he incurred no official censure and no private fault; thrice he bore diplomatic missions without disgracing his sovereign's charge; whether the gentleman was worthy or not, he received all with humble courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: From infancy to retirement he served eleven rulers over more than seventy years without official censure or private fault. Thrice he bore diplomatic missions without disgracing his sovereign's charge, and received every man, worthy or not, with humble courtesy.

sentences.zh: 晚年背傴，時人咸曰鄭傴不迂。

translations.literal: In his later years his back was bent; people of the time all said "Bent Zheng" was not obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: In old age his back was bent; people said "Bent Zheng" was never stubborn.

sentences.zh: 平生交友之中無怨隙，親族之間無愛憎，恬和自如，性尚平簡，及致政歸洛，甚愜終焉之志。

translations.literal: Among friends in his life there was no rancor; among kin there was no favoritism or hatred. He was tranquil and at ease, by nature inclined to plain simplicity, and when he left office and returned to Luoyang he was deeply content with his wish to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Among friends he left no rancor; among kin no favoritism or hatred. Tranquil and at ease, he loved plain simplicity, and when he retired to Luoyang he was deeply content to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 天福五年秋，寢疾而卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Tianfu he took to his bed with illness and died at the age of eighty.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the fifth year of Tianfu he fell ill in bed and died, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made right vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王權，字秀山，太原人，積世衣冠。

translations.literal: Wang Quan, styled Xiushan, was a native of Taiyuan, a family of official robes for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Quan, courtesy name Xiushan, was from Taiyuan, a family of officials for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖起，官至左僕射、山南西道節度使，冊贈太尉，謚曰文懿，唐史有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qi rose to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Military Governor of the Shannan West Circuit; by edict posthumously awarded Grand Marshal, posthumous title Wényì; the Tang histories have his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qi rose to left vice director of the secretariat and military governor of Shannan West; posthumously made grand marshal with the posthumous title Wényì; the Tang histories record him.

sentences.zh: 祖龜，浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gui was Observation Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gui had been observation commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 父蕘，右司員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Rao was Vice Director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rao had been vice director of the right secretariat.

sentences.zh: 權舉進士，解褐授秘書省校書郎、集賢校理，歷左拾遺、右補闕。

translations.literal: Quan passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving the sackcloth he was appointed Collator in the Secretariat and Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and served successively as Left Reminder and Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Quan passed the jinshi, became collator in the secretariat and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and served as left reminder and right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 梁祖革命，御史司憲崔沂表為侍御史，遷兼職方員外郎知雜事。

translations.literal: When the founder of Liang changed the dynasty, Censor-in-Chief Cui Yi memorialized him as Attending Censor; he was transferred to concurrently serve as Vice Director of the Bureau of Appointments in charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's founder changed the dynasty, censor-in-chief Cui Yi recommended him as attending censor; he was then made vice director of appointments in charge of miscellaneous cases.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，召入翰林為學士，在院加戶部郎中、知制誥，歷左諫議大夫、給事中，充集賢殿學士判院事，俄拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned to the Hanlin as Academician; while in the academy he was added Director of the Household Registration Bureau and charged with drafting edicts, served successively as Left Advisory Censor and Drafting Attendant, acted as Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies adjudicating academy affairs, and soon was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he entered the Hanlin as academician, added director of household registration and charge of drafting edicts, served as left advisory censor and drafting attendant, headed the Hall of Assembled Worthies academy, and soon became censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗平梁，以例出為隨州司馬，會赦，量移許州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang conquered Liang, by precedent he was sent out as Military Governor's Aide at Suizhou; he met an amnesty and was transferred in reduced rank to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong of Tang overthrew Liang he was demoted by precedent to aide at Suizhou; after an amnesty he was transferred in reduced rank to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 月餘，入為右庶子，遷戶兵吏三侍郎、尚書左丞、禮部尚書判銓。

translations.literal: After more than a month he entered as Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent, then was transferred to the three vice ministries of Revenue, War, and Personnel, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Minister of Rites adjudicating selection.
translations.idiomatic: After a month he became right guardian of the heir apparent, then vice minister of revenue, war, and personnel, left vice director of the secretariat, and minister of rites heading selection.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，權知貢舉，改戶部尚書，華資美級，罕不由之。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he acted as head of the metropolitan examination, then was changed to Minister of Revenue. Splendid qualifications and fine ranks rarely did not pass through his hands.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he oversaw the metropolitan examination, then became minister of revenue. Splendid posts and fine ranks rarely escaped his hand.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，轉兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, he was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he was made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 天福中，命權使於契丹，權以前世累為將相，未嘗有奉使而稱陪臣者，謂人曰：「我雖不才，年今耄矣，豈能遠使於契丹乎！

translations.literal: During Tianfu he was ordered to serve as envoy to the Khitan. Quan, whose forebears for generations had been generals and chief ministers, had never known a diplomatic mission in which one called oneself a subordinate minister. He told others: "Though I lack talent, I am now old—how can I go on a distant mission to the Khitan!
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he was ordered envoy to the Khitan. Quan, whose forebears for generations had been generals and chief ministers, had never known a mission in which one styled oneself a subordinate minister. He said, "Though I lack talent, I am old now—how can I go on a distant mission to the Khitan!

sentences.zh: 違詔得罪，亦所甘心。

translations.literal: To disobey the edict and incur guilt is also what I would accept."
translations.idiomatic: To disobey the edict and accept punishment is what I would willingly bear."

sentences.zh: 」由是停任。

translations.literal: For this his appointment was halted.
translations.idiomatic: For this his appointment was halted.

sentences.zh: 先是，宰相馮道使於契丹才回，權亦自鳳翔冊禮使回，故責詞略曰：「若以道路迢遙，即鸞閣之臺臣亦往；

translations.literal: Earlier, Chief Councillor Feng Dao had just returned from a mission to the Khitan, and Quan had also just returned from Fengxiang as envoy for investiture rites. Therefore the reprimand in brief said: "If the road is far and remote, then the terrace ministers of the Phoenix Pavilion have also gone;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Feng Dao had just returned from a Khitan mission, and Quan had just returned from Fengxiang as investiture envoy. The reprimand in brief said, "If the road is far, terrace ministers of the Phoenix Pavilion have also gone;

sentences.zh: 若以筋骸衰減，即鳳翔之冊使才回。

translations.literal: if sinews and bones are weakened, then the investiture envoy from Fengxiang has just returned.
translations.idiomatic: if one's frame is weakened, the investiture envoy from Fengxiang has just returned.

sentences.zh: 既黷憲章，須從殿黜」云。

translations.literal: Having violated the statutes, dismissal from court is required."
translations.idiomatic: Having violated the statutes, dismissal from court is required."

sentences.zh: 其實權不欲臣事契丹，故堅辭之，非避事以違命也。

translations.literal: In truth Quan did not wish to serve the Khitan as a subordinate minister, and therefore firmly declined—it was not evading duty to disobey orders.
translations.idiomatic: In truth Quan did not wish to serve the Khitan as a subordinate minister and firmly declined; it was not evading duty to disobey orders.

sentences.zh: 逾歲授太子少傅致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was made junior tutor to the heir apparent and retired.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，以疾卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he died of illness at the age of seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the sixth year he died of illness, aged seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈左僕射。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 韓惲，字子重，太原晉陽人。

translations.literal: Han Yun, styled Zizhong, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yun, courtesy name Zizhong, was from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖俊，唐龍武大將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jun was General of the Dragon Martial Guard under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jun had been general of the dragon martial guard under Tang.

sentences.zh: 祖士則，石州司馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shize was Military Governor's Aide at Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shize had been military governor's aide at Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 父逵，代州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Kui was Prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui had been prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 惲世仕太原，昆仲為軍職，惟惲親狎儒士，好為歌詩，聚書數千卷。

translations.literal: The Han family for generations served at Taiyuan; his brothers held military posts, but only Yun was intimate with scholar-gentlemen, loved composing songs and poems, and collected several thousand volumes.
translations.idiomatic: The Hans for generations served at Taiyuan; his brothers held military posts, but Yun alone was close to scholars, loved poetry, and collected thousands of books.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，後唐莊宗納其妹為妃，初為嫡室，故莊宗深禮其家，而惲以文學署交城、文水令，入為太原少尹。

translations.literal: During Qianning, Later Tang's Zhuangzong took Yun's younger sister as consort; she was at first the principal wife, so Zhuangzong deeply honored the family. Yun was appointed by literary merit as Magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui, then entered as Vice Governor of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianning Zhuangzong of Later Tang took Yun's younger sister as consort; she was first principal wife, so Zhuangzong deeply honored the family. Yun was appointed by literary merit magistrate of Jiaocheng and Wenshui, then vice governor of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定趙、魏，為魏州支使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei, Yun served as branch commissioner at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong pacified Zhao and Wei, Yun served as branch commissioner at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，授右散騎常侍，從駕至洛陽，轉尚書戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong acceded, Yun was appointed Right Regular Attendant, accompanied the imperial procession to Luoyang, and was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong took the throne Yun was made right regular attendant, followed the court to Luoyang, and became vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 天成初，改秘書監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was changed to Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiancheng he was made director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 俄而馮道為丞相，與惲有同幕之舊，以惲性謹厚，尤左右之，尋遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon Feng Dao became chief councillor; he and Yun had old ties from the same staff. Because Yun's nature was careful and sincere, Feng especially favored him, and soon Yun was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Feng Dao became chief councillor; he and Yun had served on the same staff. Feng especially favored Yun for his careful, sincere nature, and soon made him minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 丁內憂，服闋，授戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother; when the mourning period ended he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother he was made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 明宗晏駕，馮道為山陵使，引惲為副使。

translations.literal: When Mingzong died, Feng Dao was commissioner for the imperial tomb and brought Yun in as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong died Feng Dao headed the tomb commission and made Yun his deputy.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，以充奉之勞，授檢校尚書右僕射、絳州刺史，逾年入為太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, for his labors in the funeral service he was appointed Supernumerary Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Prefect of Jiangzhou; after more than a year he entered as Household Companion to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qingtai, for his funeral labors he was made supernumerary right vice director of the secretariat and prefect of Jiangzhou; after a year he became household companion to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，以惲先朝懿戚，深加禮遇，除授貝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended, because Yun was a close kinsman of the former court, he was treated with deep courtesy and appointed Prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he treated Yun, a close kinsman of the former court, with deep courtesy and made him prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 時範延光有跋扈之狀，惲懼其見逼，遲留不敢赴任，高祖不悅，復授太子賓客，尋改兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At that time Fan Yanguang showed an overbearing manner; Yun feared he would be pressed and delayed, not daring to take up his post. Gaozu was displeased, again appointed him Household Companion to the Heir Apparent, and soon changed him to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang then showed an overbearing manner; Yun feared pressure and delayed, not daring to take up his post. Gaozu was displeased, made him household companion to the heir apparent again, then minister of war.

sentences.zh: 天福七年夏，車駕在鄴，惲病腳氣，卒於龍興寺，時年六十餘。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Tianfu, when the imperial carriage was at Ye, Yun suffered from foot ailment and died at Longxing Temple at somewhat over sixty years of age.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the seventh year of Tianfu, while the court was at Ye, Yun fell ill with foot ailment and died at Longxing Temple, aged somewhat over sixty.

sentences.zh: 李懌，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Li Yi was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi was from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖褒，唐黔南觀察使。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bao was Observation Commissioner of Qiannan under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bao had been observation commissioner of Qiannan under Tang.

sentences.zh: 父昭，戶部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Zhao was Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao had been minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 懌幼而能文，進士擢第，解褐為校書郎、集賢校理、清河尉。

translations.literal: Yi from youth could write; he passed the jinshi examination and upon leaving the sackcloth was made Collator, Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and Assistant Magistrate of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote well from youth, passed the jinshi, and upon leaving office dress became collator, collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and assistant magistrate of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 入梁，歷監察御史、右補闕、殿中侍御史、起居舍人、禮部員外郎、知制誥，換都官郎中，賜緋，召入翰林為學士，正拜舍人，賜金紫，仍舊內職。

translations.literal: Entering Liang, he served successively as Investigating Censor, Right Remonstrator, Attending Censor within the Palace, Recorder of the Sovereign's Movements, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and charged with drafting edicts; was transferred to Director of the Capital Bureau, granted crimson robes, summoned to the Hanlin as Academician, formally appointed Drafter, granted gold seal and purple robes, and retained his inner-court duties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as investigating censor, right remonstrator, palace attending censor, recorder of the sovereign's movements, vice director of rites, and drafter of edicts; became director of the capital bureau, received crimson robes, entered the Hanlin as academician, was formally made drafter, received gold seal and purple robes, and kept his inner-court post.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平汴、洛，責授懷州司馬，遇赦，量移孟州，入為衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Bian and Luo, Yi was punished by appointment as Military Governor's Aide at Huaizhou; he met an amnesty and was transferred in reduced rank to Mengzhou, then entered as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong pacified Bian and Luoyang Yi was demoted to aide at Huaizhou; after an amnesty he was transferred in reduced rank to Mengzhou, then became vice director of the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 天成初，復拜中書舍人，充翰林學士，在職轉戶部侍郎右丞，充承旨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was again appointed Secretariat Drafter and served as Hanlin Academician; while in office he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and Right Vice Director, and acted as Drafting Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiancheng he was again made secretariat drafter and Hanlin academician; while in office he became vice minister of revenue and right vice director, and served as drafting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時常侍張文寶知貢舉，中書奏落進士數人，仍請詔翰林學士院作一詩一賦，下禮部，為舉人格樣。

translations.literal: At that time Regular Attendant Zhang Wenbao oversaw the metropolitan examination. The Secretariat memorialized to fail several jinshi and also requested an edict that the Hanlin Academy draft one regulated poem and one fu, send them to the Ministry of Rites, and use them as models for candidates.
translations.idiomatic: Regular attendant Zhang Wenbao then oversaw the metropolitan examination. The secretariat memorialized to fail several jinshi and asked that the Hanlin draft one regulated poem and one fu for the Ministry of Rites as models for candidates.

sentences.zh: 學士竇夢徵、張礪輩撰格詩格賦各一，送中書，宰相未以為允。

translations.literal: Academicians Dou Mengzheng, Zhang Li, and others each drafted one model poem and one model fu and sent them to the Secretariat; the chief councillors did not approve them.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians Dou Mengzheng, Zhang Li, and others each drafted one model poem and one model fu and sent them to the secretariat; the chief councillors did not approve.

sentences.zh: 夢徵等請懌為之，懌笑而答曰：「李懌識字有數，頃歲因人偶得及第，敢與後生髦俊為之標格！

translations.literal: Mengzheng and the others asked Yi to do it. Yi smiled and answered: "Li Yi knows only so many characters; a few years ago I passed the examination by chance through others' favor—how dare I set the standard for the brilliant young talents of later generations!
translations.idiomatic: They asked Yi to do it. Yi smiled and said, "Li Yi knows only so many characters; I passed the examination a few years ago by chance through others' favor—how dare I set the standard for the brilliant young men of today!

sentences.zh: 假令今卻稱進士，就春官求試，落第必矣。

translations.literal: If I were called a jinshi today and went to the Ministry of Rites to seek examination, I would certainly fail."
translations.idiomatic: If I were called a jinshi today and went to the Ministry of Rites to sit the examination, I would certainly fail."

sentences.zh: 格賦格詩，不敢應詔。

translations.literal: As for model fu and model regulated verse, I dare not comply with the imperial edict."
translations.idiomatic: As for model fu and model verse, I dare not obey the edict."

sentences.zh: 」君子多其識大體。

translations.literal: Men of virtue widely praised his grasp of the larger principle.
translations.idiomatic: Men of virtue widely praised his sense of the larger principle.

sentences.zh: 天福中，自工部尚書轉太常卿，歷禮部、刑部二尚書，以多病留司於洛下，不交人事。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he moved from Minister of Works to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, served successively as Minister of Rites and Minister of Punishments, and because of many illnesses remained on duty in Luoyang without engaging in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he moved from minister of works to director of imperial sacrifices, served as minister of rites and minister of punishments, and because of frequent illness remained on duty in Luoyang without engaging in worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 開運未，遇契丹入洛，家事罄空，尋以疾卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun, when the Khitan entered Luoyang, his household property was utterly emptied; soon he died of illness at somewhat over seventy years of age.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyun, when the Khitan entered Luoyang, his household was stripped bare; soon he died of illness, aged somewhat over seventy.
